value.first: Nights 1-3: set up her room as the fun place before bedtime, not just for sleep. Get her a new pillow or blanket she picks out. Do the same wind-down you do now, but finish it in her room: bath, two books, lights low. Sit right beside her bed until she's asleep. She may cry or climb out; walk her back calmly, same words each time. Expect the first two nights to be the hardest.
value.second: Nights 4-7: same routine, but move your chair a little further from her bed each night, toward the door. Keep the walk-back-to-bed the same and boring on purpose, no long talks. If she wakes and comes to you, take her straight back with the same phrase. A hard night 4 or 5 after a good night 3 is normal and not a sign it's failing.
value.third: After that: aim to say goodnight from the doorway and leave while she's still awake. Most families see it settle in one to two weeks once the room feels like hers. Keep her bedtime and wake time steady, even on weekends. If she's still waking scared or inconsolable most nights after two weeks, or the resistance is getting worse rather than easing, worth raising with your doctor.
